A Duration or Instant operand never reaches this guard: instantArithmetic always returns for an Instant, and durationArithmetic already decides every Duration case whose other operand fits int.
The earlier compatibleClasses check passes only when one class is in the base chain of the other. A chain that contains number ends at number, so the two classes are both numeric or both not.

The mutant sends a value that is not a literal expression to literalOf. literalOf returns a value only for a node that holds a direct string, number, true, false, or null token. The parser gives such a token directly only to LiteralExpr and to an import path, so an options value of any other kind gives undefined, as the guard does. An absent value (the shorthand field { on }) makes kindOf return undefined, which is not LiteralExpr, so literal is undefined again and the report is the same. A syntax error stops the check before this rule, so an error recovery node cannot reach it.

reason: The mutant is A || (B && C) || D, where A is that self is not local, B is that the body is undefined, C is that the body is not a call, and D is that the role of the builtin of the body is not container. The builtin helper returns undefined for a body that is undefined or not a call, so recursionRoleOf gives reject and D is true. B and C each imply D, so the swap never changes the result.

The wider guard already rejects every case that the mutant drops. When capacity is undefined, value is undefined, so the second operand is true and the next operand, !Number.isSafeInteger(value), is true too. When value is not a number, Number.isSafeInteger(value) is false, so the third operand rejects it. Only a safe positive integer reaches the accept path, in both forms.

Three inputs separate the mutant. A binding function reaches the edit, but its binding type closes its sets, so the check after the edit rejects it. A function with no written result has a declaration/005 diagnostic in its span when exported, and an open set with no missing entry when not exported. An arrow with no body is a broken declaration, which the broken guard rejects.

Only an annotation of the kind binding separates the mutant. A binding function takes its effects from the binding type and ignores the written clauses, so the edit leaves the missing entries in place and the check after the edit rejects it. The binding test in tests/editor_actions_test.ts passes under the mutant (checked by hand).

The publish step in check_project.ts drops every body diagnostic of a broken declaration, so such a function has no contract diagnostic. The edit then removes no diagnostic, and the delta.removed.length === 0 guard rejects the action.

The checker anchors one function diagnostic at the start of the function span: the SchemaError rule for inferred inputs in check_expr.ts. Its code is failure-contract/001, which this condition excludes. Every other function diagnostic starts at the name or later.

The parser numbers nodes in post-order: newNode runs when a leaf or a finished node is added. Node 0 is the first leaf of the file. An ArrowExpr child of a declaration always follows its own => leaf and the const keyword, so its id is never 0.

The guard skips a Duration or Instant operand, but no such operand reaches it. numericIdentityOf returns only a named type, so named is never undefined. instantArithmetic returns before this call for every Instant operand. For a Duration operand, durationArithmetic returns before this call whenever the other operand fits int, and the world table fixes the body of Duration at int, so the test fits(unnamed, body) here is the same as the integral test there. Without the guard the function still returns undefined for every input that reaches it.

The condition is the first term of a conjunction that ends in ms.some(...). Array.prototype.some on an empty array is false, so for ms.length == 0 the whole conjunction is false in both forms. For a non-empty array both comparisons are true.

The callback runs only in the branch where records is true, that is, where ms.every(m => m.kind === "record") holds. No member has a kind other than record there, so the guard m.kind !== "record" never fires and its return value is never read.

The compatibleClasses check earlier in this method returns mismatch unless the class chain of one class contains the other class. The chain of l then ends with the chain of r, or the reverse. A chain contains number only as its last entry, because number has no base. So l and r are both numeric or both not numeric, and && and || give the same value.

The only two calls of callbackResult follow the test decode === undefined || encode === undefined in the same || chain, which short-circuits and returns before either call. So fn is never undefined in callbackResult, and the line fn === undefined: return false cannot run.
